story_of_day.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin plan a joint meeting in China next week
story_of_day.story: The White House says Trump, Xi and Putin will hold an unprecedented three-way meeting in China next week, around APEC. Trump will raise 'reduction of nuclear weapons'. Al Jazeera says a nuclear treaty and the US war on Iran are among the priority topics for Beijing and Moscow.
story_of_day.so_what: Having all three in one room is a big deal in itself. Watch for any sign that Moscow and Beijing get something on Iran or Ukraine in return for arms talks.

cards.headline: US floats Donbas for NATO membership, Zelensky says
cards.story: Zelensky says US envoys, for the first time, asked whether Ukraine would give up the Donbas in exchange for a NATO path. He says any security deal could go to a referendum. He also says Russia rejected a ceasefire on energy infrastructure.
cards.so_what: This is a big shift in what Washington is willing to ask of Kyiv. A referendum would make it very hard for Zelensky to say yes quickly.

last_time.text: Europe had just picked five countries for the talks; now the US has put a land-for-NATO idea on the table.

cards.headline: Audit says Bangladesh's growth was overstated for a decade
cards.story: A government forensic audit found GDP growth was inflated by up to 1.3 percentage points a year since FY15, with data manipulation across seven sectors under the previous government. The statistics bureau plans to change the GDP base year. Other numbers are weak too: bad loans are 32.78% of bank lending, and tax revenue is more than Tk50,000cr short for July to October.
cards.so_what: The economy is smaller and weaker than the old figures said, just as the budget gap widens. The garment unrest adds to it: BGMEA says 147 factories with about 300,000 workers are shut, and owners threaten more closures if workers don't return.

last_time.text: Owners were due to decide on closing 210 factories; they have now issued a closure ultimatum, while the audit adds a new data shock.

cards.headline: The UN counts 25 seafarers killed around Hormuz
cards.story: The UN says 25 seafarers have died in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Israel war on Iran began, and says the situation 'cannot become the new normal'. Iran reports three more vessels hit mines. Qatar and Turkey have also signed a mutual defence pact, which analysts see as deterrence.
cards.so_what: Shipping risk in the Gulf is not fading, even with oil supply recovering. It keeps insurance costs and the oil risk premium alive.

last_time.text: Qatar and Turkey had just signed their pact; since then the UN has put a human toll on the Hormuz fighting.

cards.money_angle: Brent closed at $95.84, up from $92.17 on 9 November.

watch.title: The China summit next week
watch.text: Whether the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting produces anything on nuclear arms, Iran or Ukraine, and whether Zelensky answers the Donbas idea.

takes_review.text: I said not to chase oil lower on deal headlines. No deal was signed, Trump said the US doesn't need one, and Brent is $95.84 against $92.17 then. The wrong-if condition (a signed deal with Brent under $88) did not happen.
